system.name: Snowflake Cortex Analyst
system.version: Cortex Analyst REST API, inline semantic model (22 base tables, quoted identifiers)

declarations.artifacts: snowflake_agent/captures/snowflake_cortex_captures_run{1,2,3}.jsonl (organizer-side; per-task question, generated SQL, returned rows, latency and the verbatim Analyst response). runs/snowflake_run{1,2,3}.jsonl carry the SQL-track re-execution, runs/snowflake_run{1,2,3}_score/ and runs/snowflake_3run_score/ the verdicts.
declarations.notes: COMMERCIAL BAND: Cortex Analyst is a managed product that brings its own undisclosed model, so this is NOT a scaffold comparison against the four controlled arms, which all run gpt-5.6-luna. It belongs with Claude Code and Databricks Genie. SQL-TRACK, like every other arm: Cortex Analyst emits complete SQL with literal values, so the harness re-executes that SQL on the single reference warehouse rather than trusting the rows Snowflake returned. This matters because the Snowflake tenant holds its own load of the data; re-execution on the reference snapshot is what makes the number comparable to the rest of the board. The Snowflake DDL is column-for-column identical to the reference warehouse (22 tables, 373 columns, same names, order and types), and only the dialect is bridged, by snowflake_sql_compat.to_duckdb. A statement that will not translate is left alone and allowed to fail; a silently repaired query would inflate the score. Capture health: 149/149 recorded in all three runs, with 129, 129 and 130 tasks returning rows from Snowflake. SQL-track re-execution answered 142, 141 and 144 (95.3%, 94.6%, 96.6%); the remainder are 5/6/3 tasks where Analyst returned no SQL, 2 per run that failed to execute, and 15/14/16 that executed to an empty result. Single-turn only: the 41 tier-9 multi-turn turns were not attempted and score as failures, which is why execution accuracy over the 190-task denominator (59.1%) sits below the 149-task single-turn figure (71.1% consistent). One Analyst call per question, with no tool loop and no view of the rows it returns: 414 of the 447 task-runs generated SQL on the first call. The harness re-asks only when Analyst replies in prose instead of SQL (14 task-runs needed one retry, 4 needed two, 1 needed three, and 14 record no value because Analyst errored before any attempt). That is a retry for a missing answer, not the agent revising against results. The semantic model is inlined with every request (107,964 characters, 22 base tables) rather than staged, so each task is independent and no cross-task state accumulates. Temperature is null because the Analyst API exposes no temperature control. Run-to-run variance is low (std 0.8pp on the 190-task figure) and tier 7 was a clean 10/10 in all three runs. An earlier set of Snowflake captures exists from 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-04 against a pre-v1.3 corpus; it is archived, excluded, and must not be scored against v1.3 gold. COST IS ACCOUNT-METERED AND ESTIMATED, NOT PER-TASK BILLED: the Analyst REST response carries no token or cost field, so nothing per-task was recorded. The figure is derived from SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.METERING_DAILY_HISTORY for 2026-09-15, the day all three runs ran: 34.505 credits of AI_SERVICES (Cortex Analyst inference) plus 1.9 credits on CORTEX_BENCH_WH, the warehouse these runs used, for executing the generated SQL. A second warehouse on the account that day, COMPUTE_WH at 0.4 credits, is excluded as unrelated. 36.405 credits over 447 task-runs at $2.00/credit gives $0.1629 per task and $0.2290 per correct answer. Inference is 94.8% of it; the SQL execution is nearly free by comparison. One honest caveat. (1) EDITION: $2.00/credit is the Standard rate, confirmed against the account. Multiply by 1.5 for Enterprise or 2.0 for Business Critical if this is ever re-run on a different account. (2) NOT THE SAME METER AS OTHER ROWS: Vanna and LangChain are billed per token by OpenAI, Claude Code's figure is API-equivalent rather than billed, and this one is credit-metered at the account level across a whole day. Three different meters in one column; compare within a band, not across. Tokens are not reported because Cortex Analyst is billed per message, so Snowflake does not meter tokens for it and none can be obtained. BILLING IS PER MESSAGE, NOT PER TOKEN, and the attribution reconciles exactly. CORTEX_ANALYST_USAGE_HISTORY records 515 billed messages against 34.505 credits, which is 0.067000 credits per message -- a flat rate, exact to three decimals, so question complexity and the size of the inlined semantic model do not affect what is charged. Every one of the 34.505 credits is Cortex Analyst; nothing else on the account contributed. The 515 messages account for the 447 task-runs completely: 447 tasks at one message each, 25 further messages from recorded no-SQL retries, 42 from the 14 task-runs that hit no_sql_exhausted and burned the full MAX_NO_SQL_RETRIES of 3, and 1 smoke test. Nothing is unaccounted. RETRY OVERHEAD IS 13%: 68 of the 515 messages were retries rather than first attempts, and the 42 spent on exhausted tasks returned no SQL at all, so they were paid for and produced nothing. A caller that gave up after one retry instead of three would have spent about 5% less for the same score. CHAINED MULTI-TURN, 2026-09-17: this row now covers all 190 tasks. The 41 tier-9 turns are no longer skipped and are no longer fed an authored gold prior -- each turn receives the agent's OWN SQL from the immediately preceding turn of that session, right or wrong and unrepaired. Pass^N and Pass@N are therefore over 190, not 149: every system now attempts every task, so the old 'only count what it took on' denominator no longer applies. Comparing this row's percentage with a pre-2026-09-17 one compares two denominators. See ERRATA E-2026-09-17-13.
